# Booster: everything in one file

> Booster plans and runs PHP and Laravel upgrades one hop at a time on Rector, gates every hop with your tests on the target PHP, and never commits or pushes for you.

The README and the Markdown twin of every page, joined. The index is https://booster.apps.wayne.edu/llms.txt. Written by Squire's agent-ready kit; do not edit.

---

## README

Source: https://github.com/waynestate/booster/blob/HEAD/README.md

## Booster

**Boosts your versions.** One dose at a time, and every dose gets a stamp.

**Not to be confused with:** Booster moves an app to a newer PHP or framework version; Pinstripe's Rector set only modernises code within the PHP version the app already runs.

Checks: `composer ci` (the same command runs on GitLab and GitHub).

Development happens on Wayne State's GitLab; this repository is a release mirror. Changes land there first.

> A booster shot keeps your immunity current. This one keeps your PHP current, and it stings less.

Front page: [`site/index.html`](https://github.com/waynestate/booster/blob/HEAD/site/index.html), a static page you can open in a browser or serve from `site/`.
On Citadel it is served by the raw-PHP deploy layer in [`deploy/`](https://github.com/waynestate/booster/blob/HEAD/deploy/): a Squire kit whose front controller serves `site/` behind HELMET's security headers. For local development, keep serving `site/` directly.

Booster is WELD's upgrade tool. It plans the hops that take a WSU PHP app from the PHP or Laravel version it runs now
to one the version policy still supports, and it runs them one at a time: [Rector](https://getrector.com) rewrites the
code, Booster raises the constraints in `composer.json`, and the app's own tests must pass on the target PHP before the
next hop starts. It stands on `rector/rector` and `driftingly/rector-laravel` and adds only the ordering, the review
threshold, the gate, the advisory scans and a few WSU recipes.

Booster edits your working copy and prints a report. It never commits to, pushes or opens a merge request on your app (the only merge requests it opens are its own hop-data refresh on Booster itself): a person reads
the diff and merges it.

### Where it fits in WELD

WELD is the Wayne State application stack. Booster is its upgrade layer.

| Part | Job |
|---|---|
| WayneUI (project 0) | The interface layer every other part builds on |
| CREED | The version policy (`policy.json`) Booster reads |
| PROCTOR | Measures an app against that policy; the gate runs it before the first hop and after the last |
| Preflight | The CI templates |
| SESAME | Auth; Booster can swap `wayne-cas` for it |
| HELMET | The baseline runtime |
| Pinstripe | The coding standard |
| Sourdough | The starters |
| Booster | This project: moves apps forward |

It works for all five permutations of the stack: raw PHP, raw PHP with a Vue SPA, Laravel with Blade, Laravel with
Blade and Vue islands, and Laravel with Inertia and Vue.

### Install

Booster needs PHP 8.3 or newer, but the app it upgrades does not: Rector runs from Booster's own `vendor/`, so an app
on PHP 7.4 is rewritten by a Rector that runs on 8.3 or newer.

Linux and macOS:

```
git clone https://github.com/waynestate/booster.git
cd booster && composer install
bin/booster --version
```

Windows (PowerShell, no bash or WSL needed):

```
git clone https://github.com/waynestate/booster.git
cd booster; composer install
php vendor\bin\booster --version
```

No PHP on the machine? Run it in Docker (the path after `-v` is where your app lives):

```
docker run --rm -v "${PWD}:/booster" -w /booster composer:2 composer install --no-interaction
docker run --rm -v "${PWD}:/booster" -v "C:\path\to\app:/app" -w /booster php:8.4-cli php bin/booster plan --path=/app
```

The `run` command's test gate starts Docker itself, so it needs a Docker daemon on the machine that runs Booster.
When Booster itself runs in a container, use `--skip-gate` and run the tests yourself. Node hops run `npm` in a
`node:26` container, so they need the same daemon but no Node installed on the machine.

### Single-file download

Booster also ships as a single-file PHAR, so Preflight and apps without Composer access can run it as one file. Every
version tag publishes it: the GitLab release carries `booster.phar` as an asset, and the GitHub release at
github.com/waynestate/booster carries the same file as an attachment. Download it from either release page and run it
with `php booster.phar`.

You can also build it from any commit, with the script for your OS (both need Docker, and no PHP or Composer on the
host):

Windows (PowerShell):

```
.\scripts\build-phar.ps1
```

Linux / macOS:

```
scripts/build-phar.sh
```

Each script writes `build/booster.phar` and verifies it by printing Booster's version.

Every command works from the phar. `detect`, `plan`, `hops` and `init` read only what is bundled inside it. `run`
copies Rector, its `config/rector.php` and `docker/` out of the phar into a temp directory first, because Rector and
`docker build` are child processes that cannot be pointed at a `phar://` path; the temp directory is removed when the
command exits.

### Quick start

```
booster detect --path=../my-app        # which of the five permutations, and which versions
booster plan   --path=../my-app        # the ordered hops to a supported version
booster scan   --path=../my-app --php=8.0   # what will break on that PHP; advisory, changes nothing
booster run    --path=../my-app --dry-run   # the diffs Rector would make; changes nothing
booster run    --path=../my-app        # apply the plan, one hop at a time, with a test gate
```

The one-command form for a forced image upgrade:

```
booster run --path=../my-app --goal=php-74-to-84
```

A plan for the bundled Laravel 10 example app on PHP 8.2 looks like this (the order keeps the app on a PHP and
Laravel pair Laravel supports at every step):

```
$ booster plan --path=examples/laravel-blade --today=2026-10-29

BOOSTER plan for examples/laravel-blade
  app type: laravel-blade
  PHP: 8.2 -> 8.5
  Laravel: 10 -> 13
  PHPUnit: 10 -> 13
  policy: waynestate/creed 0.1.3 (today 2026-10-29)

1. phpunit-10-to-11  [target-image-tests]
   Move PHPUnit 10 tests to PHPUnit 11.
2. laravel-10-to-11  [target-image-tests]
   Move a Laravel 10 app to Laravel 11.
3. laravel-11-to-12  [target-image-tests]
   Move a Laravel 11 app to Laravel 12.
4. php-82-to-83  [target-image-tests]
   Move PHP 8.2 code to PHP 8.3.
   Removed between PHP 8.2 and PHP 8.3: none found.
5. phpunit-11-to-12  [target-image-tests]
   Move PHPUnit 11 tests to PHPUnit 12.
6. laravel-12-to-13  [target-image-tests]
   Move a Laravel 12 app to Laravel 13.
7. php-83-to-84  [target-image-tests]
   Move PHP 8.3 code to PHP 8.4.
   Removed between PHP 8.3 and PHP 8.4: none found.
8. phpunit-12-to-13  [target-image-tests]
   Move PHPUnit 12 tests to PHPUnit 13.
9. php-84-to-85  [target-image-tests]
   Move PHP 8.4 code to PHP 8.5.
   Removed between PHP 8.4 and PHP 8.5: none found.

Will break on PHP 8.3: no findings.

PHPStan on PHP 8.5: 5 findings.
   app/Models/Post.php:7 [class.notFound] Class App\Models\Post extends unknown class Illuminate\Database\Eloquent\Model.
   app/Models/Post.php:9 [missingType.property] Property App\Models\Post::$casts has no type specified.
   tests/PostTest.php:18 [property.onlyWritten] Property App\Tests\PostTest::$repository is never read, only written.
   tests/PostTest.php:27 [staticMethod.deprecated] Call to deprecated method isType() of class PHPUnit\Framework\Assert:
https://github.com/sebastianbergmann/phpunit/issues/6052
   tests/PostTest.php:33 [method.alreadyNarrowedType] Call to method PHPUnit\Framework\Assert::assertNotNull() with PHPUnit\Framework\MockObject\Rule\AnyInvokedCount will always evaluate to true.
```

### Commands

| Command | What it does |
|---|---|
| `booster detect` | Reads `composer.json` and `package.json`; prints the app type, PHP, Laravel, PHPUnit, Vue, Node and Boost |
| `booster plan` | Prints the ordered hops, the warnings (including which direct dependencies block which hops), a removals line per PHP hop, an advisory PHPCompatibility scan of the first PHP hop's target and a PHPStan scan at the destination PHP. Changes nothing. |
| `booster scan` | Advisory scans of one PHP version: PHPCompatibility by default, `--removals` for removed functions, `--phpstan` for static analysis. Exits 0 even with findings |
| `booster run` | Runs the plan. `--dry-run` previews every hop |
| `booster hops` | Lists every hop Booster knows |
| `booster init` | Writes the coding-tab playbooks to `.agents/skills`; `--check` exits 1 when they are stale |

Options shared by `plan` and `run`:

| Option | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `--path` | The app (default `.`) |
| `--format` | `text` (default) or `json` |
| `--policy` | CREED's `policy.json`. Default: `BOOSTER_POLICY`, then the copy in the `waynestate/creed` package |
| `--today` | Override today's date (`YYYY-MM-DD`) so runs are repeatable |
| `--goal` | Shorthand such as `php-74-to-84` (sets `--from-php` and `--to-php`) |
| `--from-php`, `--from-laravel` | Say what the app runs on when the manifest does not |
| `--to-php`, `--to-laravel`, `--to-phpunit` | The target. Default: the newest version the policy supports today (PHPUnit: the newest that runs on the target PHP) |
| `--sesame` | Include the `wayne-cas` to SESAME swap |
| `--skip` | A hop id to leave out (repeat it) |
| `--no-package-check` | Skip the Packagist dependency check (for offline use) |
| `--with-node` | include the Node front-end hops (Node pin, Mix to Vite, Tailwind, Vue) even when you passed a target version. Without it, any of `--goal`, `--to-php`, `--to-laravel`, `--to-phpunit`, `--from-php` or `--from-laravel` leaves those hops out, and the plan prints: "Node front-end hops were left out because you passed a target version: . Add --with-node to include them." |

Options for `plan`:

| Option | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `--no-scan` | Skip the advisory scans (PHPCompatibility and PHPStan) |

Options for `scan`:

| Option | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `--path` | The app (default `.`) |
| `--php` | Required. The PHP version to ask about (`major.minor`, one Booster knows) |
| `--removals` | List uses of functions and constructs removed in PHP up to `--php`, instead of the PHPCompatibility scan |
| `--phpstan` | Also run the PHPStan scan (Pinstripe preset) at the same PHP version |
| `--format` | `text` (default) or `json` |

Options for `run`:

| Option | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `--dry-run` | Show the diffs; change nothing; skip git, the baseline and the gate. A Laravel hop without `vendor/` is marked incomplete |
| `--max-changes` | Hard limit on files changed per hop, with no prompt (`0` lifts the limit). Without it, a hop over the review threshold of 200 files asks first when interactive, or stops |
| `--memory-limit` | Memory limit for the Rector process (for example `2G`), or `-1` for no limit (default `2G`) |
| `--skip-gate` | Do not run the tests in the target image after each hop, or the PROCTOR check at the end (skips the baseline too) |
| `--image` | Run the gate in this Docker image instead of building `booster-target` (it needs `php` and `composer` on `PATH`): one name, a `{php}` template or a version map (below) |
| `--allow-failing-baseline` | Continue when the baseline fails; later gate failures are labelled as pre-existing |
| `--allow-dirty` | Run even when the working copy has uncommitted changes |
| `--test-command` | What runs the app's tests in the image (default `composer test`, else `vendor/bin/phpunit`) |
| `--proctor-command` | An extra command run in the image after the tests, for example a PROCTOR check |
| `--proctor-advisory` | Report the PROCTOR result but do not fail the run on it |

Exit codes: `0` pass, `1` the baseline failed, a hop was capped, errored or failed its gate, or the PROCTOR check
found new findings, `2` bad usage (bad option, unreadable policy, broken `composer.json`, a target the policy does
not support).

#### The PHPCompatibility scan

`plan` ends with an advisory scan: PHP_CodeSniffer runs the PHPCompatibility standard over the app and asks what will
break on the PHP version the first PHP hop lands on. The findings are hints for the person doing the upgrade, never a
gate: they do not change the exit code, and a scan that cannot run (missing tooling, a crash) is reported as "could
not run" while the plan still prints in full. `--no-scan` skips both advisory scans.

The scan is optional. Booster looks for a PHP_CodeSniffer that carries the PHPCompatibility standard, trying the app's
own `vendor/bin/phpcs`, then Booster's `vendor/bin/phpcs`, then `phpcs` on the PATH. When none of them has the
standard, the scan reports a skip and the plan goes on. To turn it on, install the packages into the app:

```
composer require --dev phpcompatibility/php-compatibility:"^10.0@alpha"
```

Before the require line, approve the installer plugin once:

```
composer config allow-plugins.dealerdirect/phpcodesniffer-composer-installer true
```

Composer asks for approval of `dealerdirect/phpcodesniffer-composer-installer`, the plugin that registers the
PHPCompatibility standard with PHP_CodeSniffer. Without the approval, Composer blocks the plugin, the standard never
registers, and the scan skips with a message that names this fix. The command writes `allow-plugins` into the app's
own `composer.json`. That is an app-side change the person who wants the scan chooses to make; Booster never edits
the app's `composer.json`.

The scan ignores `vendor/`, `node_modules/` and `storage/`, because those hold third-party code and generated files,
not the app's. It reads the app only and changes nothing. `booster scan --path=../my-app --php=8.0` runs the same scan
on its own, for any PHP version Booster knows, and exits 0 even when it finds a wall of removed functions.

#### The PHPStan scan

`plan` ends with a second advisory scan: PHPStan runs over the app at the destination PHP version, using Pinstripe's
`base.neon` preset. The findings are hints for the person doing the upgrade, never a gate: they do not change the
exit code, and a scan that cannot run is reported with the fix that enables it, while the plan still prints in full.
`--no-scan` skips it.

The scan is optional. Booster looks for a PHPStan binary, trying the app's own `vendor/bin/phpstan`, then Booster's
`vendor/bin/phpstan`, then `phpstan` on the PATH, and for the preset it tries the app's vendor tree and Booster's.
When either is missing, the report names the fix:

```
composer require --dev phpstan/phpstan waynestate/pinstripe
```

It ignores `vendor/`, `node_modules/` and `storage/`, reads the app only and changes nothing. `booster scan
--path=../my-app --php=8.5 --phpstan` runs the same scan on its own, for any PHP version Booster knows, and exits 0
even when it finds a wall of missing types.

#### The dependency check

Before the hops print, `plan` (and `run`) asks Packagist about each direct third-party dependency in the app's
`composer.json`: what is its newest stable release, and can that release still be installed at each hop's
destination? Only plain `require` and `require-dev` entries count; PHP, extensions (`ext-*`, `lib-*`), Laravel
itself (`laravel/framework`, its `illuminate/*` components) and PHPUnit are Booster's own business, so they are
skipped.

The answer is advisory, like the scans: a package that cannot follow the plan does not drop the hop. It adds a
warning that names the package, the hop it blocks, and what to do about it:

```
acme/legacy-auth 2.3.0 supports Laravel up to 10 (or PHP up to 8.3), so it blocks laravel-10-to-11. Replace or upgrade it first.
```

A package whose newest release requires several `illuminate/*` components is judged by the loosest of those
constraints, the one that allows the most Laravel versions. Abandoned packages get their own warning (`acme/old is
abandoned (use acme/new instead).`). Packages the check cannot reach are reported as `Not checked:
(offline).` or `(VCS repository).`, and the plan goes on. In JSON output every package lands under
`package_checks`, with the fields `package`, `newest`, `blocks`, `abandoned` and `checked`.

The check fetches from `repo.packagist.org` and from any composer-type repository the app declares in
`composer.json`; VCS repositories are never fetched. `--no-package-check` skips the whole check, for offline use.

#### The baseline

Before the first hop, `run` runs the app's own tests on the PHP the app is on now, in the same `booster-target:`
image the gate uses. The point is to tell "Booster broke it" from "it was already broken": a red baseline means the
suite was red before any change, so a later red gate is not proof of a bad hop. The baseline is recorded in the report
(`passed`, `failed` or `skipped`, with the exit code and the last 20 lines of output).

- A red baseline stops the run before the first hop, with a non-zero exit. `--allow-failing-baseline` lets it go on;
  each later gate failure is then labelled "the baseline was already failing" in the text and JSON output.
- `--skip-gate` and `--dry-run` skip the baseline (reported as `skipped`), so a dry run never starts Docker.
- A Mix app's `public/mix-manifest.json` is a build artifact, not committed source: a fresh clone has no manifest, so
  the suite can be red before any hop. Build the assets before the baseline (the app's usual `npm ci && npm run
  build`), or pass `--allow-failing-baseline` knowing why.

#### What a hop does

On PHP hops a pre-pass runs first: PHP 4 era `$a = &new Foo();` becomes a plain assignment, because PHP 7 and newer
refuse to compile the old spelling and Rector would never get a parse tree. The report lists the rewrites per file
under `Pre-pass fixes:`.

1. Rector runs as a dry run. If it reports errors, the run stops before anything is written. So does a hop that would
   change more than 200 files, unless an interactive run confirms it after showing the per-rule summary; an explicit
   `--max-changes` is a hard limit that never asks. An empty Rector report usually means the process ran out of memory,
   and the message points at `--memory-limit`.
2. Rector runs for real, with only that hop's rules.
3. `composer.json` is edited: the `php` or `laravel/framework` constraint is raised, and `config.platform.php` moves
   with it when the app already pins it. Booster never runs `composer update` and never creates the key.
4. The gate runs the app's tests inside `booster-target:-`, a container built from `docker/Dockerfile`
   on the PHP the hop moves to. The stamp is a short hash of the recipe, so an edited `docker/Dockerfile` rebuilds
   the image instead of reusing a stale one. The image carries the extension set Citadel's apps run with: intl,
   ldap, soap, zip, gd, pdo_mysql, mysqli, bcmath, pcntl, exif, redis, imagick and oci8. The first build downloads
    Oracle Instant Client for oci8, so it takes a few minutes; later hops reuse the image. Pass `--image` to run the
    gate in your own image instead (below). A red gate stops the run and leaves the changes in place so you can read
    them (`git checkout .` undoes them). To check the image itself,
    `scripts/check-target-image.sh` (or its Windows twin `check-target-image.ps1`) builds it for each PHP version and
    verifies its extension list; it needs Docker and a few minutes per version, so it is not part of `composer ci`.

The `--image` value names the image the baseline and every gate run in, and it takes three shapes:

- One name, used for the baseline and every gate: `--image myapp/gate:8.4`.
- A template whose `{php}` is replaced with the PHP version of that baseline or gate:
  `--image registry/php-apache:{php}` gates the 8.1 hop on `registry/php-apache:8.1` and the 8.2 hop on
  `registry/php-apache:8.2`.
- A map of PHP version to image, for a fleet whose images do not follow one pattern:
  `--image 8.0=legacy/php:7.4,8.1=registry/php-apache:8.1`. A map without the version a baseline or hop lands on
  stops the run before the first hop and names the fix; a template never misses.

Booster never builds a `--image` image: it must exist locally or be pullable, and each resolved image is pulled at
most once per run. On an arm64 Mac, Citadel's published images such as `citadel/php-apache:8.5r3` are amd64 only:
pass an arm64 build via `--image`, or set `DOCKER_DEFAULT_PLATFORM=linux/amd64` and let Docker emulate.
`booster-target` itself builds natively on arm64. And the old-PHP images (7.1 through 8.0) point apt at
archive.debian.org, so they get no security updates: they exist to run the app's tests on the way up, not to serve
traffic.

`run` refuses to start on a working copy that is not under git or has uncommitted changes, so the upgrade diff stands
alone. `--dry-run` has no such limit.

A dry run previews every hop against the original tree, so the same file can appear in several hops. The report ends
with the number of unique files and a reminder that nothing was applied. A Laravel hop whose app has no `vendor/`
cannot see the framework's classes, so its preview is marked incomplete and the report says to run `composer install`
first.

Three hops edit manifests instead of code. `node-pin-24` sets `engines.node` in `package.json` and writes `.nvmrc`,
then the app's usual gate applies. `mix-to-vite` converts a simple `webpack.mix.js` to Vite (below) and asks for a
build gate, which runs `npm ci` and `npm run build` in the `node:26` container before the app's tests.
`tailwind-3-to-4` runs the official `@tailwindcss/upgrade` tool in the Node container, then pins `tailwindcss` to
`^4.1`, adds the matching Vite or PostCSS plugin, and removes `autoprefixer` and `postcss-import`, which Tailwind 4
folds in; plugins listed in `tailwind.config.js` and `@apply` inside Vue SFC `` blocks stay manual work, and
the hop says so.

Vue 2 to Vue 3 is staged. `vue-26-to-27` moves the front end to the last Vue 2 release, which carries the Vue 3
reactivity API; `vue-27-to-compat` switches to the `@vue/compat` build; `vue-compat-codemod` runs the
`vue-upgrade-tool` codemod and keeps every manual item it lists. `vue-2-to-3` is the playbook that stands in for all
three: skipping it skips them, and a person finishes the job, because Rector does not read Vue.

#### Hops Booster knows

Thirty-two hops: PHP one minor at a time from 5.5 to 8.5, Laravel one major at a time from 5.8 to 13 and PHPUnit one
major at a time from 9 to 13, each list read from `data/versions.json` and trimmed to the majors whose Rector ruleset
is installed ([Hop data](#hop-data)). Then the recipes: `cas-to-sesame` (renames the `wayne-cas` classes to SESAME's
compatibility classes and swaps the Composer requirement; planned with `--sesame`, and left out with a warning when
the plan ends below PHP 8.3, which SESAME needs); `node-pin-24` (planned for any app with a `package.json` that does
not already floor Node at the hop data's target, 26 today: sets `engines.node` to `>=26` and writes `.nvmrc`, ahead
of the front-end hops); `mix-to-vite` (planned when the app has a `webpack.mix.js` and the plan lands on Laravel 9 or
newer, after `node-pin-24`: writes `vite.config.js`, swaps `laravel-mix` for `vite` and `laravel-vite-plugin` in
`package.json`, renames `MIX_` keys to `VITE_` in `.env.example`, rewrites Blade `mix()` script and link tags into one
`@vite([...])` line per layout when every referenced asset maps to a Mix entry, and deletes `webpack.mix.js`; the
simple shape only: `mix.js`, `.vue()`, `.sass()`, `.postCss()`, `.version()` and `if (mix.inProduction()) {
mix.version(); }` (dropped with a note, since Vite hashes production assets), anything else is refused by name, a
Vue 2 front end must take `vue-2-to-3` first, and `withoutMix()` calls are listed for a manual rename to
`withoutVite()`); `tailwind-3-to-4` (planned when `package.json` carries `tailwindcss` below 4, after `node-pin-24`
and `mix-to-vite`: runs the official `@tailwindcss/upgrade` tool, pins `tailwindcss` to `^4.1`, adds the matching
Vite or PostCSS plugin and removes `autoprefixer` and `postcss-import`); and the Vue 2 to Vue 3 stage,
`vue-26-to-27`, `vue-27-to-compat` and `vue-compat-codemod`, with the `vue-2-to-3` playbook standing in for all three.
`booster hops` prints them all.

Booster plans only what the policy supports as a target. Moving to PHP 8.1 is refused because 8.1 is past security
support; passing through it on the way to a newer version is fine.

### Configuration

| Variable | Meaning | Default |
|---|---|---|
| `BOOSTER_POLICY` | Path to CREED's `policy.json` | the copy in the `waynestate/creed` package |

Booster reads the policy straight from the `waynestate/creed` package in its own `vendor/`, so there is no copy to
drift: `composer update waynestate/creed` is the whole refresh. `--policy` and `BOOSTER_POLICY` still override it for
one run.

`.env.example` holds the placeholder. Booster reads no secrets, makes no network calls of its own and talks to no
Citadel host. Everything it prints from an app (file names, diffs) has control characters stripped.

When Rector runs, Booster passes it a few `BOOSTER_*` variables of its own (the app path, the sets, the PHP target).
They are internal; do not set them.

### Laravel hops and `vendor/`

rector-laravel needs Laravel's classes to recognise a model or a controller. For a Laravel hop Booster loads the app's
own `vendor/autoload.php` when it exists, so run `composer install` in the app first. PHP hops never load the app's
autoloader. An app with no `vendor/` still gets a plan and the hops that do not need Laravel's classes.

For an Inertia/Vue app, each Laravel hop also raises the Inertia constraints the app already carries:
`inertiajs/inertia-laravel` and `@inertiajs/vue3` move to the constraint the hop data pairs with the target major
(`^2.0` for Laravel 11 and newer). Booster never adds a package the app does not have, and below Laravel 11 it pins
nothing and says so, because the hop data carries no constraint there.

### Hop data

`data/versions.json` holds the version facts Booster plans against: the PHP, Laravel and PHPUnit chains, the PHP range
each Laravel major supports, the PHPUnit floor each Laravel major ships, the Node floor the `node-pin-24` hop writes,
and the fixed Tailwind pin and Inertia constraint tables the front-end hops use. The file ships inside the PHAR. A new
major appears in the file as soon as its feed says so; Booster offers a hop for it only once Rector ships a ruleset
for it, and a plan toward a major without one stops there with a warning instead of failing.

`bin/refresh-hop-data.php` rewrites the file from the public feeds (Packagist for PHPUnit and Laravel, endoflife.date
for Laravel's supported PHP ranges, npm for the Vite packages) plus CREED's policy for what counts as supported:

```
php bin/refresh-hop-data.php             # fetch the feeds, rewrite the file, print what changed
php bin/refresh-hop-data.php --check     # offline CI check: validate the shape, then compare the frozen feeds
php bin/refresh-hop-data.php --online    # compare against the live feeds without writing the file
php bin/refresh-hop-data.php --offline tests/fixtures/hop-feeds --today 2026-10-29 --dry-run
```

The refresh is deterministic for a given set of feeds and date, and it never touches the recipes: writing a playbook
for a new hop stays human work. `composer ci` ends with the offline `--check`: it validates the file's shape against
the bundled policy, then recomputes it from the frozen feeds in `tests/fixtures/hop-feeds` as of the file's
`generated_on` date, so the check itself needs no network. A scheduled pipeline runs the hop data robot,
`bin/hop-data-bot.php`, against the live feeds; when a feed moved while the file slept, the robot opens (or updates)
a merge request on Booster itself with the new file, and a person merges it. [MAINTAINING.md](https://github.com/waynestate/booster/blob/HEAD/MAINTAINING.md) covers
the token the robot needs.

### Checks

Maintainers: how to build, test and release this project, and where its data comes from, is in [MAINTAINING.md](https://github.com/waynestate/booster/blob/HEAD/MAINTAINING.md).

```
composer ci
```

runs `composer validate --strict`, PHPUnit, Pint, PHPStan (Pinstripe's raw preset, inlined; `waynestate/pinstripe` is
a dev requirement and supplies the preset the advisory scan uses), `composer audit`, the hop data check and the
agent-ready check. Nothing needs PHP on the host:

```
docker run --rm -v "${PWD}:/app" -w /app composer:2.10.3 sh -c "composer install --no-interaction && composer ci"
```

`contract/expectations.json` says what Booster must detect, plan and change for each example app in `examples/`;
`tests/ContractTest.php` enforces it with the real Rector, so a Rector release that changes a hop shows up in CI.

### Proof

Proof runs against real Wayne State applications are on a private site, [proof.apps.wayne.edu/booster](https://proof.apps.wayne.edu/booster/), behind a Wayne State employee sign-in.

Proven how: the first full run with the gate on took a Laravel 12 app from PHP 8.2 to 8.4 in two hops, each gated by
the app's 197-test suite, and it is written up in [research/booster-e2e-gate.md](https://github.com/waynestate/booster/blob/HEAD/research/booster-e2e-gate.md).

### Status

Version 1.0. See [CHANGELOG.md](https://github.com/waynestate/booster/blob/HEAD/CHANGELOG.md) for what changed, [OPEN_QUESTIONS.md](https://github.com/waynestate/booster/blob/HEAD/OPEN_QUESTIONS.md) for what stays
open, and [BEST_PRACTICES.md](https://github.com/waynestate/booster/blob/HEAD/BEST_PRACTICES.md) for the rules Booster follows.

MIT, Wayne State University, Enterprise Applications.

Source: https://booster.apps.wayne.edu/

PHP and Laravel upgrades · WELD stack

## BOOSTER

Boosts your versions.

A booster shot keeps your immunity current. This one keeps your PHP current, and it stings less. Booster works out the hops from the PHP or Laravel version your app runs today to one CREED still supports, and runs them one at a time. [Rector](https://getrector.com) rewrites the code and Booster raises the constraints in `composer.json`. Your tests have to pass on the new PHP before the next hop starts.

- **One hop** per dose
- **200 files** review threshold per hop
- **0** commits made for you

[Watch a plan launch](https://booster.apps.wayne.edu/#record) [Install](https://booster.apps.wayne.edu/#install)

**Works alongside [WELD](https://weld.apps.wayne.edu/).** WELD and [Sourdough](https://sourdough.apps.wayne.edu/) start new apps. Booster is for the apps you already have.

![Booster logo: a syringe that is also a rocket, gold flame below](https://booster.apps.wayne.edu/brand/booster-avatar-512.png)

- **Altitude**: PHP 8.5
- **Stage**: 6 of 6
- **Gate**: target-image tests

Dose by dose

### A stamp for each hop that passes.

These are Booster's plans for the example apps in `examples/`, written up like a vaccination card. Pick an app and press Run the plan.

Form B-01 · Version immunization record

#### examples/laravel-blade

- **App type**: laravel-blade
- **Course**: PHP 8.2 → 8.5 · Laravel 10 → 13 · PHPUnit 10 → 13
- **Policy**: waynestate/creed 0.1.3
- **Next booster due**: 17 Mar 2028

1. 01 `phpunit-10-to-11` Move PHPUnit 10 tests to PHPUnit 11. PHP 8.2 · Laravel 10 booster-target:8.2 Gate passed PHP 8.2 28 Oct 2026
2. 02 `laravel-10-to-11` Move a Laravel 10 app to Laravel 11. PHP 8.2 · Laravel 11 booster-target:8.2 Gate passed PHP 8.2 28 Oct 2026
3. 03 `laravel-11-to-12` Move a Laravel 11 app to Laravel 12. PHP 8.2 · Laravel 12 booster-target:8.2 Gate passed PHP 8.2 28 Oct 2026
4. 04 `php-82-to-83` Move PHP 8.2 code to PHP 8.3. PHP 8.3 · Laravel 12 booster-target:8.3 Gate passed PHP 8.3 28 Oct 2026
5. 05 `phpunit-11-to-12` Move PHPUnit 11 tests to PHPUnit 12. PHP 8.3 · Laravel 12 booster-target:8.3 Gate passed PHP 8.3 28 Oct 2026
6. 06 `laravel-12-to-13` Move a Laravel 12 app to Laravel 13. PHP 8.3 · Laravel 13 booster-target:8.3 Gate passed PHP 8.3 28 Oct 2026
7. 07 `php-83-to-84` Move PHP 8.3 code to PHP 8.4. PHP 8.4 · Laravel 13 booster-target:8.4 Gate passed PHP 8.4 28 Oct 2026
8. 08 `phpunit-12-to-13` Move PHPUnit 12 tests to PHPUnit 13. PHP 8.4 · Laravel 13 booster-target:8.4 Gate passed PHP 8.4 28 Oct 2026
9. 09 `php-84-to-85` Move PHP 8.4 code to PHP 8.5. PHP 8.5 · Laravel 13 booster-target:8.5 Gate passed PHP 8.5 28 Oct 2026

RESULT: PASS Review with `git diff`, run your own checks, then commit. Booster never commits or pushes.

The overlap

### Never on a pair Laravel doesn't support.

Booster mixes the PHP and Laravel hops so the app is on a supported pair after every hop. Laravel 10 runs on PHP 8.1 to 8.3, 11 on 8.2 to 8.4, 12 on 8.2 to 8.5, 13 on 8.3 or newer. If you ask for a pair that can't exist, Booster refuses before anything runs.

The target also has to be one CREED's policy still supports. A plan can pass through PHP 8.1, but it can't stop there:

```
$ bin/booster plan --path=examples/raw-php --to-php=8.1
PHP 8.1 is past security support; pick a version the policy still supports.
exit 2
```

supported pair not a pair Laravel supports the Laravel and PHP hops for Laravel 10 on PHP 8.2

Grid of Laravel versions 10 to 13 against PHP 8.1 to 8.5. The path starts at Laravel 10 on PHP 8.2, moves to Laravel 11 and then 12 on PHP 8.2, PHP 8.3, Laravel 13, then PHP 8.4 and PHP 8.5.

Inside one dose

### Four steps before the next stage fires.

1. T−4
   ### Dry run and review
   Rector previews the hop. If it reports errors, the run stops before anything is written. So does a hop over the review threshold of 200 files: an interactive run shows the per-rule summary and asks first, and `--max-changes` sets a hard limit instead.
2. T−3
   ### Rector for real
   Rector runs with only that hop's rules, from Booster's own `vendor/`. That's how an app on PHP 7.4 gets rewritten by a Rector running on 8.3 or newer.
3. T−2
   ### Raise the constraint
   The `php` or `laravel/framework` constraint in `composer.json` goes up, and `config.platform.php` moves with it. Booster never runs `composer update`.
4. T−1
   ### The gate
   Before the first hop your tests run once on the app's current PHP as the baseline; a red one stops the run unless you pass `--allow-failing-baseline`. After each hop they run inside `booster-target:<php>`, built from `docker/Dockerfile` on the PHP the hop moves to, and after the last hop PROCTOR checks the upgraded app against CREED's policy, blocking only on findings the upgrade introduced. If a red baseline names a missing Mix or Vite manifest, build the front-end assets first. A failure stops the run and leaves the changes for you to read. `git checkout .` undoes them.

Not every hop is Rector. `node-pin-24` pins Node 26 in `package.json` and writes `.nvmrc`; `mix-to-vite` converts a simple `webpack.mix.js` and moves the build to Vite. The Vue 2 to 3 move is staged: `vue-26-to-27`, `vue-27-to-compat` and `vue-compat-codemod`, with the `vue-2-to-3` playbook standing in for all three. Rector doesn't read Vue, so a person works those steps. The plan also flags PHP 7.4 to 8.0 as the hop that needs the most review.

The commands

### The whole kit.

There's also `scan`, which reports what will break on a given PHP (`--removals` for removed functions, `--phpstan` for static analysis) and always exits 0. Exit codes: **0** pass · **1** the baseline failed, or a hop was capped, errored or failed its gate · **2** bad usage or a target the policy does not support.

**detectWhich of the five stack shapes, and which versions**

$ bin/booster detect --path=examples/vue-spa path examples/vue-spa app_type raw-php-vue composer_json yes php 8.0 laravel unknown phpunit unknown vue 2 node unknown mix_file no wayne_cas no boost no

**planThe ordered hops, the warnings and the scans. Changes nothing.**

$ bin/booster plan --path=examples/raw-php --today=2026-10-29 BOOSTER plan for examples/raw-php app type: raw-php PHP: 7.4 -> 8.5 policy: waynestate/creed 0.1.3 (today 2026-10-29) 1. php-74-to-80 \[target-image-tests\] Move PHP 7.4 code to PHP 8.0. Give this hop the most review time. Removed between PHP 7.4 and PHP 8.0: none found. 2. php-80-to-81 \[target-image-tests\] Move PHP 8.0 code to PHP 8.1. Removed between PHP 8.0 and PHP 8.1: none found. 3. php-81-to-82 \[target-image-tests\] Move PHP 8.1 code to PHP 8.2. Removed between PHP 8.1 and PHP 8.2: none found. 4. php-82-to-83 \[target-image-tests\] Move PHP 8.2 code to PHP 8.3. Removed between PHP 8.2 and PHP 8.3: none found. 5. php-83-to-84 \[target-image-tests\] Move PHP 8.3 code to PHP 8.4. Removed between PHP 8.3 and PHP 8.4: none found. 6. php-84-to-85 \[target-image-tests\] Move PHP 8.4 code to PHP 8.5. Removed between PHP 8.4 and PHP 8.5: none found. Will break on PHP 8.0: no findings. PHPStan on PHP 8.5: 3 findings. src/Legacy.php:20 \[missingType.parameter\] Method Example\\Legacy::className() has parameter $object with no type specified. src/Legacy.php:22 \[return.type\] Method Example\\Legacy::className() should return string but returns class-string|false. src/Legacy.php:25 \[parameter.implicitlyNullable\] Deprecated in PHP 8.4: Parameter #1 $label (string) is implicitly nullable via default value null.

**runRuns the plan; --dry-run previews every hop**

$ bin/booster run --path=examples/raw-php --to-php=8.2 --dry-run BOOSTER dry run (nothing was changed) Baseline: SKIPPED (no gate in this run). 1. php-74-to-80: PREVIEWED (1 files) Largest risk hop: loose comparison of numbers and strings changed, many warnings became thrown errors, and arithmetic on arrays throws. Write or extend tests before applying this hop; only tests and review find behaviour changes here. --- src/Legacy.php --- Original +++ New - public function \_\_construct(string $name) + public function \_\_construct(private string $name) - return strpos($text, 'admin') !== false; + return str_contains($text, 'admin'); - return get_class($object); + return $object::class; 2. php-80-to-81: PREVIEWED (0 files) Dry run: nothing was changed. mysqli now throws on errors by default; PDO on MySQL returns native int and float types; htmlspecialchars() now escapes single quotes. Passing null to a non-nullable built-in parameter is deprecated: check the log after the run. 3. php-81-to-82: PREVIEWED (0 files) Dry run: nothing was changed. Unique files across hops: 1. Later hops were previewed against the original tree, so the same file can appear in several hops. RESULT: PASS Dry run: these changes were previewed, none were applied.

**hopsEvery hop Booster knows**

$ bin/booster hops php-55-to-56 Move PHP 5.5 code to PHP 5.6. php-56-to-70 Move PHP 5.6 code to PHP 7.0. php-70-to-71 Move PHP 7.0 code to PHP 7.1. … one PHP minor at a time … php-84-to-85 Move PHP 8.4 code to PHP 8.5. laravel-5.8-to-6 Move a Laravel 5.8 app to Laravel 6. … one Laravel major at a time … laravel-12-to-13 Move a Laravel 12 app to Laravel 13. phpunit-9-to-10 Move PHPUnit 9 tests to PHPUnit 10. … one PHPUnit major at a time … phpunit-12-to-13 Move PHPUnit 12 tests to PHPUnit 13. cas-to-sesame Swap the wayne-cas package for SESAME using its compatibility classes. node-pin-24 Pin the app to Node 26: set engines.node in package.json and write .nvmrc. mix-to-vite Move a simple Laravel Mix front end to Vite (simple webpack.mix.js files only). tailwind-3-to-4 Move a Tailwind CSS 3 front end to Tailwind CSS 4 with the official upgrade tool. vue-26-to-27 Move a Vue 2.6 front end to Vue 2.7, the last Vue 2 release, which carries the Vue 3 reactivity API. vue-27-to-compat Move a Vue 2.7 front end to Vue 3 through the @vue/compat build. vue-compat-codemod Run the vue-upgrade-tool codemod over the front end and keep every manual item it lists. vue-2-to-3 Move a Vue 2 front end to Vue 3 (playbook only; Rector does not read Vue). \[playbook\]

**initWrites the coding-tab playbooks to .agents/skills**

$ bin/booster init --path=../my-app Wrote 33 playbooks, 33 changed. $ bin/booster init --path=../my-app --check # exits 1 when a playbook is stale, so CI notices

Get the shot

### Install, then plan.

Booster needs PHP 8.3 or newer. The app it upgrades does not: an app on PHP 7.4 is fine. The gate in `run` starts Docker itself, so the machine needs a Docker daemon.

**Linux and macOS**

```
git clone https://github.com/waynestate/booster.git
cd booster && composer install
bin/booster detect --path=../my-app
bin/booster plan   --path=../my-app
bin/booster run    --path=../my-app --dry-run
bin/booster run    --path=../my-app
```

**Windows**

```
# PowerShell; no bash or WSL needed
git clone https://github.com/waynestate/booster.git
cd booster; composer install
php bin\booster detect --path=..\my-app
php bin\booster plan   --path=..\my-app
php bin\booster run    --path=..\my-app --dry-run
php bin\booster run    --path=..\my-app
```

**Docker, no PHP**

```
# inside the booster clone; the path after the second -v is your app
docker run --rm -v "${PWD}:/booster" -w /booster composer:2 composer install --no-interaction
docker run --rm -v "${PWD}:/booster" -v "/path/to/app:/app" -w /booster php:8.4-cli php bin/booster plan --path=/app
```

When Booster itself runs in a container, pass `--skip-gate` to `run` and run the tests yourself.

The one-shot form, for a forced image upgrade

`bin/booster run --path=../my-app --goal=php-74-to-84`

On Packagist

It's `waynestate/booster` on Packagist. Give it its own folder, not your app's `vendor/`, because it needs PHP 8.3 even when your app doesn't. Clone it as above, or run `composer create-project waynestate/booster booster ^1.0`.

Single file

Every version tag publishes `booster.phar` as a release asset on GitLab and GitHub. Run it with `php booster.phar`; every command works from the phar. Preflight and apps without Composer access use this form.

For your coding agent

### Standing orders.

Six prompts for whatever coding agent you use: one to get started, then one for each app shape. Copy one, or open it in OpenCode, Claude Code, Codex or ChatGPT. Each starts with a plan that changes nothing, and none of them lets the agent commit for you.

#### Get started with Booster

Clones Booster next to your app, runs `detect` and `plan`, and reports back. Nothing in your app changes.

A prompt for your coding agent. Copy it as it stands:

```text
You are a coding agent planning a PHP and Laravel upgrade with Booster, for the app in this folder, at Wayne State University. Booster is the upgrade tool of WELD, the Wayne State application stack: it plans the hops from the versions the app runs today to ones CREED's version policy still supports, and runs them one at a time on Rector, with the app's own tests as the gate on each hop.

Read first:
- https://booster.apps.wayne.edu/llms.txt, the index of Booster's pages, each one as Markdown; llms-full.txt beside it holds the README with every command and option. Fetch what you need; do not work from memory.
- ADVISOR, the stack's MCP server, if it is connected: upgrade_path for this app, policy_lookup for PHP and Laravel, and read_project_docs for booster. If it is not connected, say so and work from the pages. How to add it: https://advisor.apps.wayne.edu/llms.txt
- This app's composer.json, and package.json if there is one.

Task:
1. Clone Booster into its own folder beside the app with `git clone https://github.com/waynestate/booster.git`, then run `composer install` in it. Booster needs PHP 8.3 or newer; the app does not. No PHP on the machine: use the Docker lines from the README.
2. Run bin/booster detect --path=../my-app (on Windows PowerShell, php bin\booster with ..\my-app) and say which of the five stack shapes the app is and which versions it runs.
3. Run bin/booster plan --path=../my-app and give me the ordered hops, the warnings, what will break on each hop's target PHP, and the PHPStan findings for the final target.
4. Say which hops are Rector, which edit manifests and which are playbooks a person works through.

Constraints:
- Plan only. Do not run bin/booster run, not even with --dry-run, until I say so.
- Booster never commits, pushes or opens a merge request, and neither do you: a person reads the diff and merges it.
- Ask me before you guess: a version the manifest does not state, a target the policy refuses, or anything that touches CI or a deploy.

Output: the shape and versions, the plan as a numbered list, the warnings and scan findings, then your questions.
```

#### Or write the order for your app's shape

#### Upgrade a raw PHP app

Plans the PHP hops, scans for what will break and does a dry run. The real run waits until you say so.

A prompt for your coding agent. Copy it as it stands:

```text
You are a coding agent upgrading a raw PHP app (no framework, no Vue) at Wayne State University with Booster, the upgrade tool of WELD, the Wayne State application stack.

Read first:
- https://booster.apps.wayne.edu/llms.txt, then the README in llms-full.txt beside it: Quick start, What a hop does and The baseline.
- ADVISOR, the stack's MCP server, if it is connected: upgrade_path for this app, and list_stack_rules with permutation raw-php. If it is not connected, say so and work from the pages.

Task:
1. With Booster cloned beside the app, run bin/booster detect --path=../my-app and confirm the shape is raw-php.
2. Run bin/booster plan --path=../my-app. Expect PHP hops only, one minor at a time.
3. Run bin/booster scan --path=../my-app --php=X.Y for the first hop's target and list what will break; add --removals for removed functions and --phpstan for static analysis.
4. Run bin/booster run --path=../my-app --dry-run and summarise the diffs per hop.
5. Only when I say so: bin/booster run --path=../my-app. It needs a clean git working copy and a Docker daemon for the gate, which runs `composer test` (or vendor/bin/phpunit) in the target PHP image.

Constraints:
- One hop at a time; a red gate stops the run and leaves the changes for me to read (`git checkout .` undoes them). Never commit or push.
- If a hop is over the review threshold, show me its per-rule summary before applying it. Do not use --max-changes=0 or --skip-gate without asking me.
- Ask me before you guess: a red baseline, a capped hop, or a target the policy refuses.

Output: the plan, the scan findings, the dry-run summary per hop, then your questions.
```

#### Upgrade a raw PHP app with a Vue front end

Plans the PHP hops and the Node pin, and stages the Vue 2 to 3 move: the compat build, then the codemod, with a person doing the Vue work.

A prompt for your coding agent. Copy it as it stands:

```text
You are a coding agent upgrading a raw PHP app with a Vue single-page front end at Wayne State University with Booster, the upgrade tool of WELD, the Wayne State application stack.

Read first:
- https://booster.apps.wayne.edu/llms.txt, then the README in llms-full.txt beside it: Quick start and Hops Booster knows.
- ADVISOR, the stack's MCP server, if it is connected: upgrade_path for this app, policy_lookup for Node and Vue, and list_stack_rules with permutation raw-php-vue. If it is not connected, say so and work from the pages.
- package.json and its lock file.

Task:
1. With Booster cloned beside the app, run bin/booster detect --path=../my-app and confirm the shape is raw-php-vue, with the Vue and Node versions.
2. Run bin/booster plan --path=../my-app and sort the hops: PHP hops (Rector), node-pin-24 (pins Node 26 in package.json and writes .nvmrc), and the staged Vue hops if the app is on Vue 2: vue-26-to-27 when it is below 2.7, then vue-27-to-compat and vue-compat-codemod.

4. For the Vue hops, list the playbook steps for this app: the compat build, then the codemod, keeping every manual item the codemod lists. Rector does not read Vue, so Booster changes nothing there: a person does that work.

Constraints:
- Plan and dry run only, until I say so. Never commit or push.
- Node hops run npm in a node:26 container, so they need a Docker daemon but no Node on the machine.

Output: the plan sorted into PHP, Node and Vue, the dry-run summary, the Vue playbook steps, then your questions.
```

#### Upgrade a Laravel app with Blade

Laravel and PHP hops in the order that keeps a supported pair at every step, and SESAME if the app still signs in with wayne-cas.

A prompt for your coding agent. Copy it as it stands:

```text
You are a coding agent upgrading a Laravel app with Blade views at Wayne State University with Booster, the upgrade tool of WELD, the Wayne State application stack.

Read first:

Task:
1. Run `composer install` in the app first: rector-laravel needs Laravel's classes, and a Laravel hop without vendor is only a partial preview.
2. With Booster cloned beside the app, run bin/booster plan --path=../my-app and explain the order: it keeps the app on a PHP and Laravel pair Laravel supports at every step.
3. If composer.json requires wayne-cas, run the plan again with --sesame and say what the cas-to-sesame hop renames. Only the two-factor sign-in stays manual; list that for a person.
4. Run bin/booster run --path=../my-app --dry-run and summarise the diffs per hop.

Constraints:
- Plan and dry run only, until I say so. Never commit or push.
- Booster never runs composer update; say which packages will need it after each hop.
- Ask me before you guess: a red baseline, a capped hop, or a package that blocks a Laravel major.

Output: the plan with the reason for its order, the SESAME notes if any, the dry-run summary, then your questions.
```

#### Upgrade a Laravel app with Vue islands

The Laravel and PHP hops, the Node pin, and Mix to Vite when the plan lands on Laravel 9 or newer.

A prompt for your coding agent. Copy it as it stands:

```text
You are a coding agent upgrading a Laravel app with Blade views and Vue islands at Wayne State University with Booster, the upgrade tool of WELD, the Wayne State application stack.

Read first:
- https://booster.apps.wayne.edu/llms.txt, then the README in llms-full.txt beside it: Hops Booster knows (node-pin-24, mix-to-vite, vue-26-to-27, vue-27-to-compat, vue-compat-codemod) and Laravel hops and vendor.

Task:
1. Run `composer install` in the app, then, with Booster cloned beside it, bin/booster plan --path=../my-app.
2. If the plan has mix-to-vite, say whether this webpack.mix.js is the simple shape Booster converts (mix.js, .vue(), .sass(), .postCss(), .version(), and if (mix.inProduction()) { mix.version(); }) or which call it will refuse by name. A Vue 2 front end takes the staged Vue hops first: vue-26-to-27 when it is below 2.7, then vue-27-to-compat and vue-compat-codemod.
3. Run bin/booster run --path=../my-app --dry-run and summarise the diffs, Blade layouts included.

Constraints:

```

#### Upgrade a Laravel app with Inertia

The Laravel and PHP hops and the Node pin, with the Inertia checks a person still does by hand.

A prompt for your coding agent. Copy it as it stands:

```text
You are a coding agent upgrading a Laravel app with Inertia and Vue at Wayne State University with Booster, the upgrade tool of WELD, the Wayne State application stack.

Read first:
- https://booster.apps.wayne.edu/llms.txt, then the README in llms-full.txt beside it: Quick start, Laravel hops and vendor, and Hops Booster knows.
- ADVISOR, the stack's MCP server, if it is connected: upgrade_path for this app, policy_lookup for Laravel, Node and Vue, and list_stack_rules with permutation laravel-inertia-vue. If it is not connected, say so and work from the pages.
- composer.json, package.json and its lock file.

Task:
1. Run `composer install` in the app, then, with Booster cloned beside it, bin/booster detect --path=../my-app and bin/booster plan --path=../my-app.
2. Sort the hops: Laravel and PHP (Rector), node-pin-24, and the staged Vue hops if the app is on Vue 2 (playbooks, not code changes): vue-26-to-27 when it is below 2.7, then vue-27-to-compat and vue-compat-codemod.
3. For each Laravel hop, list what to check by hand on the Inertia side: Booster has no Inertia checks per Laravel hop yet.
4. Run bin/booster run --path=../my-app --dry-run and summarise the diffs per hop.

Constraints:
- Plan and dry run only, until I say so. Never commit or push.
- A Laravel hop without vendor is only a partial preview; say so if you see one marked incomplete.
- Ask me before you guess: an inertiajs package that blocks a Laravel major, or a red baseline.

Output: the plan sorted by kind, the Inertia checks per Laravel hop, the dry-run summary, then your questions.
```

The agent reads the same pages you do: [llms.txt](https://booster.apps.wayne.edu/llms.txt) lists them, [llms-full.txt](https://booster.apps.wayne.edu/llms-full.txt) holds them all in one file, and this page has a [Markdown twin](https://booster.apps.wayne.edu/index.md). Nothing here phones home. The buttons only copy text or open the tool you picked.

Contraindications

### What Booster will not do.

Side effects are limited to the diff in your working copy. Read it, then merge it yourself.

- ### Commit, push or open a merge request
  It edits the working copy and prints a report. A person reads the diff and merges it.
- ### Start on a dirty tree
  `run` refuses a working copy that is not under git or has uncommitted changes, so the upgrade diff stands alone. Pass `--allow-dirty` if you must.
- ### Aim at an unsupported version
  An end-of-life target is refused; a security-only one comes with a warning. The dates come from CREED's `policy.json`, never from Booster's code.
- ### Run `composer update`
  It raises the constraints and stops there. You decide when to resolve them.
- ### Pass quietly
  An unreadable policy, broken JSON, missing Docker or a Rector error stops the run with exit 1 or 2.
- ### Trust your file names
  Subprocesses take argument arrays, and control characters are stripped from everything printed. It reads no secrets and makes no network calls of its own.

The care team

### Booster's place in WELD.

WELD is the Wayne State application stack. Booster is its upgrade layer, and it works for all five shapes: raw PHP, raw PHP with a Vue SPA, Laravel with Blade, Blade with Vue islands, and Inertia with Vue.

- [WayneUI](https://wayneui.apps.wayne.edu/)The interface layer under everything, this page included.
- [CREED](https://creed.apps.wayne.edu/)Writes the version policy Booster reads from the waynestate/creed package.
- [PROCTOR](https://proctor.apps.wayne.edu/)Measures an app against that policy; the gate runs it after the last hop, and `--proctor-command` overrides the check.
- [Preflight](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/)The CI templates Booster's own checks run on.
- [SESAME](https://sesame.apps.wayne.edu/)Sign-in; `--sesame` moves wayne-cas apps to it.
- [HELMET](https://helmet.apps.wayne.edu/)Security headers and session hardening.
- [Pinstripe](https://pinstripe.apps.wayne.edu/)The coding standard. Booster's PHPStan advisory scan runs against its raw preset.
- [Sourdough](https://sourdough.apps.wayne.edu/)Starts new raw PHP apps on current versions.
- [WELD](https://weld.apps.wayne.edu/)The Laravel and Vue starter, with the stack already installed.
- BoosterMoves apps forward, one dose at a time.You are here
- [Squire](https://squire.apps.wayne.edu/)Carries the release out the door.
- [Rollcall](https://rollcall.apps.wayne.edu/)Every app answers “present”, with its PHP version.
- [ADVISOR](https://advisor.apps.wayne.edu/)An MCP server your agent can ask about the stack.
- [Drawbridge](https://drawbridge.apps.wayne.edu/)The sign-in gateway, lowered on request.

Version 1.0

### Not yet given.

The five example apps prove the plumbing end to end, and the gate now ends with PROCTOR checking the result against CREED's policy. What 1.0 leaves open, from [OPEN_QUESTIONS.md](https://github.com/waynestate/booster/blob/main/OPEN_QUESTIONS.md):

- Not yet Custom WSU Rector rules beyond the CAS rename, and Rector pilot numbers on real apps
- Not yet A cas-to-sesame run against a real app; Duo two-factor stays manual work
- Decided No `booster mcp`: ADVISOR is the stack's read-only MCP server
- Decided No merge-request automation on app code; a person reads the diff and merges it
- Open The shared MySQL 5.6 database floor (question 8); the hop notes tell the reviewer to check it
